steps.step: Pat the chicken thighs dry, then rub with half the olive oil, half the lemon juice, half the garlic, the oregano, and half the salt and pepper. Let it sit at room temperature while the grill heats — resting helps the chicken cook evenly.
Toss the potatoes with the remaining olive oil, salt, and pepper, then thread them onto skewers so they don't fall through the grill grates.
Heat the grill to medium-high, about 400°F, and clean and oil the grates so the chicken skin won't stick.

Grill the potato skewers over direct heat, turning occasionally, until they pick up char marks and are tender when pierced with a knife, about 15 minutes. Move them to a cooler part of the grill to keep warm.
Place the chicken thighs skin-side down over direct heat and grill without moving them until the skin is deep golden and releases easily from the grates, about 8 minutes.
Flip the thighs, move them to a cooler part of the grill if flare-ups happen, close the lid, and keep cooking until the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 12 more minutes.
In the last two minutes, lay the lemon slices directly on the grates alongside the chicken so they soften and pick up light char.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then squeeze the charred lemon over the chicken and potatoes and serve.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for 3 minutes.
Toss the asparagus with half the olive oil, half the salt, and half the black pepper.
Brush the salmon fillets with the remaining olive oil, garlic, and lemon juice, and season with the remaining salt and pepper. Top with lemon slices.
Air fry the asparagus alone in a single layer until bright green and crisp-tender, about 6 minutes, then move it to a plate — the basket is too crowded to fit the fish alongside.
Add the salmon fillets to the basket skin-side down in a single layer and air fry until they flake easily with a fork, about 9 minutes depending on thickness.
Return the asparagus to the basket for the final minute just to warm it back through.
Scatter the dill over the salmon and asparagus and serve.
Pat the roast dry and season all over with salt and black pepper.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and sear the roast on all sides in its own rendered fat until deeply browned, about 8 minutes total — this crust is where a lot of the flavor comes from.
Remove the roast, add the onion, carrots, and potatoes to the pot, and stir them through the browned bits for a minute.

Whisk the beef broth with the tomato paste, garlic, and thyme, then pour it in. A pressure cooker doesn't lose liquid to evaporation the way a slow cooker does, so this smaller amount of broth is plenty to build steam and a rich gravy.
Nestle the roast back on top of the vegetables, seal the lid, and pressure cook on high for 60 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes before opening the valve the rest of the way — this keeps the meat from seizing up and staying tough.
Slice or shred the roast, spoon the vegetables and thickened juices over the top, and serve warm.
Pat the roast dry and season all over with salt and black pepper.
Heat a large pot over medium-high and sear the roast on all sides until deeply browned, about 8 minutes total.
Remove the roast and add the onion, carrots, and garlic to the drippings, stirring until the onion softens, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and thyme for 30 seconds, then pour in the beef broth, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot.

Nestle the roast back into the pot, bring to a gentle simmer, then cover and reduce the heat to low. A stovetop simmer needs to stay low and steady, just like a slow cooker's gentle heat, or the outside of the meat will toughen before the inside is tender.
Simmer covered, turning the roast once or twice, for about 2 hours.
Add the potatoes, tucking them into the liquid around the roast, and continue simmering covered until the potatoes are tender and the roast shreds easily with a fork, about 30 more minutes.
Slice or shred the roast, spoon the vegetables and pan juices over the top, and serve warm.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and melt the butter. Cook the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the garam masala, cumin, and paprika and toast for 30 seconds, stirring so the spices don't scorch on the hot metal.
Add the chicken thighs, tomato sauce, and salt, stirring to coat the chicken.
Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 10 minutes, then quick-release the steam.
Open the lid, check that the chicken is tender and cooked through, and stir in the heavy cream until the sauce turns silky and orange-pink.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed, then serve over rice or with warm flatbread.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and golden at the edges, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the garam masala, cumin, and paprika and toast for 30 seconds, stirring constantly so they don't burn.
Pour in the tomato sauce, add the chicken thighs and salt, and bring to a simmer. Unlike a slow cooker, a stovetop simmer needs watching — keep the heat at a gentle bubble, not a hard boil.
Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and tender, about 18 minutes.
Stir in the heavy cream and simmer uncovered for 2 more minutes until the sauce turns silky and orange-pink.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed, then serve over rice or with warm flatbread.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and cook the onion until softened, about 3 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken breasts, white beans, green chiles, chicken broth, cumin, oregano, and salt.
Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 12 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes before opening the valve the rest of the way.
Lift out the chicken breasts and shred with two forks, then return the shredded meat to the pot.
Stir in the cream cheese until it melts into the broth and the chili turns creamy.
Squeeze in the lime juice, taste for salt, and ladle into bowls.
Warm a splash of the chicken broth in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes — using broth instead of oil softens the onion just as well.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, and oregano and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the chicken breasts, white beans, green chiles, the remaining chicken broth, and salt, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently, turning the chicken once, until it shreds easily with a fork, about 20 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, shred with two forks, and return it to the pot.
Stir in the cream cheese until it melts into the broth and the chili turns creamy.
Squeeze in the lime juice, taste for salt, and ladle into bowls.
Toss the pork shoulder chunks with the cumin, oregano, chili powder, salt, and black pepper.
Set up the grill for indirect heat — coals or burners on one side only — and preheat to about 325°F.
Put the seasoned pork, onion, and garlic in a disposable foil pan, then pour the orange and lime juice over the top.

Set the pan on the cool side of the grill, close the lid, and cook low and slow the way a slow cooker would, until the pork pulls apart easily, about 3 hours. Check the coals or burner occasionally to keep the temperature steady.
Shred the pork right in the pan juices, discarding large onion pieces if you prefer.
Spread a portion of the shredded pork directly over the hot side of the grill grates for a couple of minutes per side so the edges crisp and char — the direct heat does what a broiler would.
Serve in tortillas or over rice while the crispy bits are still warm.
Set the pressure cooker to sauté and toss the pork shoulder with cumin, oregano, chili powder, salt, and black pepper directly in the pot along with the onion and garlic.
Pour the orange and lime juice over the pork.
Seal the lid and pressure cook on high for 45 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes, then open the valve the rest of the way — this keeps the pork from getting tough.
Lift the pork out of the juices and shred with two forks.

Set the pressure cooker back to sauté, return the shredded pork to the pot in a single layer, and let it sit undisturbed until the edges crisp and brown in the rendered fat, about 8 minutes, stirring once halfway.
Serve in tortillas while the crispy bits are still hot.
Toss the pork shoulder with the cumin, oregano, chili powder, salt, and black pepper.
Place the pork in a large pot with the onion and garlic, then pour the orange and lime juice over the top.

Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook at a gentle simmer, turning the pork occasionally, until it pulls apart easily, about 2 hours 30 minutes. Add a splash of water if the liquid runs low before the pork is tender.
Shred the pork right in the pot juices, discarding large onion pieces if you prefer.
Heat a large skillet over high heat and spread a portion of the shredded pork in a single layer, letting it sit undisturbed until the edges crisp and brown, about 4 minutes.
Serve in tortillas while the crispy bits are still warm.
Season the beef stew meat with salt and black pepper, then toss with the flour until lightly coated.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches until the edges darken, about 5 minutes total — this happens on the stove since a slow cooker can't sear, but it's worth the extra pan for the flavor.
Transfer the beef to the slow cooker along with the onion, garlic, carrots, and potatoes.

Stir the tomato paste and worcestershire sauce into the beef broth, then pour it over everything in the slow cooker. Use the full amount of broth here — over many hours a slow cooker loses more liquid to gentle steam than a sealed pressure cooker does.
Cover and cook on low until the beef is fork-tender and the vegetables are soft, about 7 hours (or 4 hours on high if you're short on time).
Taste for salt and black pepper, and serve in deep bowls.
Warm the vegetable broth in a small saucepan over low heat and keep it at a bare simmer nearby — adding warm broth instead of cold keeps the rice cooking at a steady pace.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and arborio rice and cook for 1 minute until the grains look glossy and toasted at the edges.

Add a ladle of the warm broth and a pinch of salt, stirring often until the liquid is mostly absorbed. Repeat, adding broth a ladle at a time, until the rice is creamy and tender but still has a slight bite, about 18 minutes total.
Stir in the parmesan cheese until the rice turns creamy. Season with black pepper and more salt if needed.
Spoon into bowls right away while it is still loose and silky.
Place the potatoes in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Boil the potatoes until just fork-tender, about 12 minutes, then use a slotted spoon to lift them into a colander to cool.
Bring the same water back to a gentle boil, add the eggs, and cook for 10 minutes for firm yolks.
Move the eggs to an ice bath to stop the cooking, then let both the eggs and potatoes cool until just warm.
Peel and chop the eggs. Halve or quarter the potatoes and add both to a large bowl with the celery, red onion, and pickle relish.
Stir in the mayonnaise and mustard. Season with salt and black pepper until it tastes bright and creamy.
Chill for a few minutes if you can, or serve slightly warm — both work.

Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds — softening these first keeps the soup from tasting raw after a long slow cook.
Transfer the onion and garlic to the slow cooker along with the canned tomatoes, vegetable broth, basil, sugar, salt, and black pepper.
Cover and cook on low until the tomatoes have broken down and the flavors have melded, about 5 hours (or 3 hours on high).
Blend the soup until smooth with an immersion blender right in the slow cooker, or carefully transfer in batches to a blender.
Stir in the heavy cream, taste for salt, and serve hot with grilled cheese or crackers.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the canned tomatoes, vegetable broth, basil, sugar, salt, and black pepper, and bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered, breaking up the tomatoes with a spoon, until the flavors deepen, about 20 minutes.
Blend the soup until smooth with an immersion blender, or carefully transfer in batches to a blender.
Stir in the heavy cream, taste for salt, and serve hot with grilled cheese or crackers.
Pat the pork chops dry and rub with olive oil.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, then coat both sides of the chops.
Heat the grill to medium-high, about 400°F, and clean and oil the grates.
Grill the chops over direct heat until good grill marks form, about 4 minutes per side.
Move the chops to a cooler part of the grill, close the lid, and continue cooking until the centers are just opaque and a thermometer reads 145°F, about 6 more minutes.
Rest on a plate for 3 minutes so the juices settle, then serve.
Preheat the oven to 400°F — 25°F hotter than the air fryer setting, since oven heat is less direct.
Pat the pork chops dry and rub with olive oil.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper, then coat both sides of the chops.
Arrange the chops on a wire rack set over a baking sheet so air circulates underneath, similar to how an air fryer basket works.
Bake until the centers are just opaque and a thermometer reads 145°F, about 20 minutes, flipping halfway.
Rest on a plate for 3 minutes so the juices settle, then serve.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss the sweet potato fries with olive oil, then sprinkle on the cornstarch, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper and toss again until evenly coated.
Spread the fries in a single layer with space between them — crowding them steams the fries instead of browning them, which matters even more in an oven than an air fryer basket.
Bake until the edges are browned and crisp, about 25 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Taste and add a pinch more salt while hot, then serve with your favorite dip.
Pat the chicken thighs very dry so the skin can crisp. Rub with olive oil.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper, then season under and over the skin.
Set up the grill for two-zone cooking — hot coals or burners on one side, nothing on the other — and heat to medium, about 375°F.
Place the thighs skin-side down over the hot side and grill until the skin is deep golden and releases easily from the grates, about 8 minutes.
Move the thighs to the cooler side, close the lid, and continue cooking until the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 20 more minutes.
Rest 3 minutes, then serve with a simple salad or roasted veg.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Pat the chicken thighs very dry so the skin can crisp. Rub with olive oil.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper, then season under and over the skin.
Set the thighs skin-side up on a wire rack over a baking sheet so air can reach the underside, the way an air fryer basket does.
Bake until the skin is deep golden and the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 35 minutes.
Rest 3 minutes, then serve with a simple salad or roasted veg.
Preheat the oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet.
Finely chop a few of the mushroom stems. Mix them with cream cheese, parmesan cheese, garlic, breadcrumbs, parsley, salt, and black pepper.
Brush the mushroom caps lightly with olive oil and fill each with the cream cheese mixture, mounding it slightly.
Arrange the mushrooms on the baking sheet and bake until the tops are golden and the mushrooms look juicy, about 18 minutes.
Cool for a minute so the filling sets, then serve warm.
Toss the bell peppers and onion with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, half the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Heat the grill to medium-high, about 400°F, and set a grill basket directly on the grates to heat up.
Grill the peppers and onion in the basket, stirring occasionally, until they soften and pick up char at the edges, about 10 minutes.
Toss the shrimp with the remaining olive oil and spices, then thread onto skewers so they don't slip through the grates.
Grill the shrimp skewers directly over the heat until pink and curled with light grill marks, about 2 minutes per side.
Warm the tortillas on the edge of the grill for a few seconds per side while the shrimp rests.
Squeeze the lime over everything and pile the shrimp and vegetables into the warm tortillas.
Heat the griddle to medium-high and drizzle 1 tablespoon of the vegetable oil onto one section.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour onto the hot section, and scramble until just set, then push to a cool corner of the griddle.

Add the remaining oil to a clear section of the griddle and stir-fry the garlic and frozen peas and carrots until hot, about 2 minutes, using your spatulas to keep everything moving on the flat surface.

Spread the cooked rice across the hot griddle in a thin layer, breaking up clumps with your spatulas, and let it sit undisturbed for a few seconds at a time so it picks up light char before flipping — the wide flat surface browns rice better than a pan can.
Push the vegetables and eggs into the rice, pour the soy sauce and sesame oil over everything, and toss together with the spatulas.
Scatter the green onions over the top, taste for salt, and serve hot straight off the griddle.
